rationale: bugs_open/198 has clobbered live site stylesheets in three waves (2026-08-04 relojistas; 08-17/19 six sites; 08-21 remortgagecalculator.uk and loanzy.uk), every run reporting success. The cause is one artefact with two writers that never read each other: webdesign-agent's render_css_from_spec builds assets/css/styles.css from the FK'd palette/layout/typography rows and git-commits it, never reading or writing css_themes.css_content; css-patch-agent appends its patch rules to css_themes.css_content and git-commits THE WHOLE ROW over that same file. install_site_composition_action.go inserts theme rows with css_content = '' deliberately (its own comment: the renderer reads composition via FKs), so a normally-composed site is born with an empty row while git serves 17-26KB. The first css-patch dispatch then appends ~100 bytes to '' and deploys the result wholesale, and every --color-* definition vanishes. Migration 318 (2026-08-05) fixed the LLM-fragment arm and is working exactly as built; what it assumed is that the row holds the stylesheet. This submission closes the remaining doors: (A) css-patch refuses to patch when its base is not a plausible, unshared stylesheet; (B) its refusals and failures stop minting 'complete'; (C) webdesign-agent persists what it renders into the row, so the two writers converge and per-site repairs stop expiring at the other writer's next run; (D) an opt-in shrink floor at the git writer refuses a payload that would replace a file with a fraction of itself. Another lane completed the one-time data backfill and built a stylesheet_gutted detector on 2026-08-21; this is the prevention half they explicitly left to this file's lane.

plan.summary: Close bugs_open/198's remaining doors at four seams: a base-integrity gate on css-patch-agent so an empty, stub or shared css_themes row can never be appended-to and deployed wholesale; honest work-item statuses so a refusal or failure stops reading as 'complete'; a persist-at-render step on webdesign-agent so the theme row tracks the file it never previously tracked; and an opt-in, default-OFF shrink floor enforced in the git-adapter, the only place that can see the file a commit is about to replace.

edits.rationale: check_has_css tests current_css.css_content != null and an EMPTY STRING is not null, so the empty-base arm passed the only existing gate in all three waves. The new gate is numeric and refuses two shapes: a base under 4096 BYTES (octet_length, not length — a file's size is bytes), and a theme row linked by more than one site. The floor is census-derived rather than chosen: measured across all 22 linked rows on 2026-08-21, healthy rows run 13,650-26,917 bytes and every clobbered or stub row ever observed is <= 2,381, so 4096 sits in the empty middle with ~3x margin either way; the fleet split is 19 PASS / 3 REFUSE with no overlap. site_count <= 1 closes the shared-row door: professional-dark is one row linked by finetuning.uk AND gaswholesalers.com, which serve different files (13,988 vs 20,271 bytes), so no backfill can make that row true for both. fail_on_non_numeric: true is deliberate — without it a missing css_len (this migration's query edit not having landed) would silently route EVERY run to the refusal arm and read as the guard working. The same file also stops the completions lying: every terminal here is a success-labelled complete_workflow, so the dispatch loop's complete_work_item stamps 'complete' whatever happened (the loancash arm minted 11 completes while doing nothing). Each non-success exit now stamps the item BEFORE its terminal via update_work_item_status, which the completion guard then skips.

This is the durable half. Every per-site repair this bug has produced — nine rows backfilled fleet-wide on 08-21, plus relojistas, idea.uk, noted, dartsonline, remortgagecalculator, loanzy — has an expiry equal to the OTHER writer's next run, because a webdesign-agent design run regenerates the file from the spec and the row goes stale again silently, with no symptom until the next patch dispatch (that agent runs roughly weekly per site: dartsonline seven times since 2026-07-06). One query_database step between generate_css and deploy_css writes the just-rendered CSS into the site's linked theme row byte-for-byte, so the row tracks the file at every render. It also makes the concept register's own DES-005 sentence true — 'empty css_content (webdesign-agent fills it at render)' describes a fill that has never existed. Four guards, each closing a way this step could itself cause harm: a 4096-byte floor (same number the consumer refuses at, so the halves cannot disagree about what a stylesheet is), origin <> 'seed' (never overwrite a library theme), exactly-one-linking-site (never push one site's CSS onto another through a shared row), and IS DISTINCT FROM (no version churn). Row-first ordering is deliberate: if the deploy then fails, the row still matches what the next css-patch deploy will ship. Fail-open on error_step (deploy_css) because failing an entire design run over a bookkeeping write would trade a live capability for a hygiene property, and 542 is the backstop — a row that fails to persist causes a REFUSAL later, never a clobber.
edits.sketch:
'{workflow,steps,persist_css_to_theme}' = {
  "action": "query_database",
  "next_step": "deploy_css",
  "error_step": "deploy_css",
  "output_field": "css_persisted",
  "config": {
    "query": "UPDATE css_themes ct SET css_content = $2, version = version + 1, updated_at = NOW(), description = 'persisted-at-render by webdesign-agent (bugs_open/198): tracks the deployed assets/css/styles.css' FROM style_collections sc, sites s WHERE sc.css_theme_id = ct.id AND s.style_collection_id = sc.id AND s.id = $1::uuid AND octet_length($2) >= 4096 AND ct.origin <> 'seed' AND ct.css_content IS DISTINCT FROM $2 AND (SELECT count(*) FROM sites s3 JOIN style_collections sc3 ON s3.style_collection_id = sc3.id WHERE sc3.css_theme_id = ct.id) = 1 RETURNING ct.id::text AS theme_id, ct.version, octet_length(ct.css_content) AS css_len",
    "params": ["site_context.site_id", "generated_css.result"],
    "output_format": "object"
  }
}

edits.rationale: The guard both lanes independently ranked first, at the only place it can exist. The chassis-side caller cannot compare against the incumbent file: GitCommitAction assembles a payload and produces it to Kafka, and nothing in the adapter protocol exposes file contents. This client holds both the new bytes and a cheap way to ask for the old ones — pathExists already GETs /repos/{o}/{r}/contents/{path} and discards the body, and that response carries `size`. The decision is a pure function so it can be driven by a table test. It fails CLOSED on a measurement error with a SEPARATE sentence from a real violation: 'lower the floor' is not a remedy for a contents API that returned 500, and sharing one sentence is how an operator disables a working guard to fix a network fault (the split the council forced on the 293 guard). The clamp at 0.95 is the page_total_text_floor lesson — a floor above 1.0 demands every commit GROW the file, refusing every write for ever while reading as 'deploys are broken'. minShrinkGuardFileBytes = 2048 keeps ratios off files too small for a ratio to mean anything, and is deliberately distinct from 542's 4096: that one asks whether a row is a plausible stylesheet, this one whether a file is big enough to judge.

Placement: after branch resolution and BEFORE the blob loop, so a refusal costs no API writes and leaves no orphan blobs, and on the DOMAIN-PREFIXED paths, which are the ones that exist in the tree. Measuring the unprefixed path is the dangerous mutation — every lookup 404s, every 404 reads as 'new file', and the guard passes the very commit it exists to refuse while still logging that it ran; there is a test whose only job is to fail under it, and it was run. Whole-commit refusal rather than per-file: the files in one request are one intended state, and letting the unrefused half land leaves the repo in a state no caller asked for. The refusal returns an error, which routes through the adapter's sendErrorResponse to a FAILED step chassis-side — loud, and (with migration 542) recorded as a failed work item rather than riding a success-labelled terminal.

One new field carries the opt-in over the wire. Zero — the value an older caller that never sets it decodes to, and the value this field takes when an OLDER ADAPTER drops it as unknown JSON — means OFF, which is the behaviour every caller had before it existed. That is what makes both deploy orders safe with no ordering constraint claimed: new chassis with old adapter sends a field that is ignored; new adapter with old chassis receives no field and enforces nothing; the guard is live only when the config key, the chassis and the adapter are all new, and each half alone is a no-op.

The chassis half is a pass-through and nothing more, following commit_message_field's shape on this same action (the prior art for an opt-in key here, DGH-007): a pure helper split out so it can be tested without a Kafka producer, key absent means byte-identical old behaviour, single call site. It reuses pruneFloorFromConfig rather than a type assertion because a JSON config, a hand-built map and a quoting seed deliver float64, int and string respectively, and reading only float64 would silently disable the guard on a config that looks correct. Clamping deliberately does NOT happen here — it lives adapter-side next to the comparison it protects, so a floor arriving from any other caller is clamped too. The key is a numeric literal, not a data-path reference, so it correctly does not belong in coordinator.go's dataRefKeys (which loop-suffixes step-output references); the comment says so, and names what would change if a *_field variant were ever added.

Ten tests over an httptest fake GitHub (the harness pattern from github_client_refrace_test.go, extended with a contents endpoint). Each names the mutation it fails under, and the two load-bearing ones were RUN as mutations, not asserted: deleting the enforcement call from CommitToRepo failed three tests, and measuring the unprefixed path failed TestShrinkFloorMeasuresThePrefixedPath and let the clobber through — which is the point, because that mutation's failure mode looks exactly like success. The properties pinned are the ones whose failure is invisible: prefixed-path measurement, fail-closed-on-measurement-error with a distinct sentence, zero contents calls when unconfigured (so 16 uninvolved carrier agents pay nothing and a contents outage cannot fail deploys that never asked for the guard), whole-commit refusal, and clamping rather than refuse-everything. The fixture sizes are the real cookly.uk incident: 504 bytes over 17,462.

Four tests for one property: a step that does not ask for the guard produces the payload it produced before the guard existed. That is what makes this safe to ship to 17 carrier agents at once, and it is exactly the kind of claim that reads as obviously true and stops being true the moment someone gives the key a sensible default — so the first test's named mutation is precisely that. The config-shape test exists because reading only float64 is the plausible simplification that would silently disable the guard on a seed-quoted value.

plan.risks: BLAST RADIUS OF THE SHARED SEAM: git_commit has 17 carrier agents (content-feed-orchestrator, css-patch-agent, deployer-agent, model-directory-publisher, nav-link-fixer, nav-updater, page-rebuild, page-rerender, pageflow-builder, report-builder, rerender-pages, rerender-site, section-editor, site-asset-renderer, site-deployer, site-work-orchestrator, webdesign-agent). Exactly ONE step opts in (css-patch-agent's deploy_css at 0.5); the other 16 agents send a byte-identical payload and make zero extra API calls, which is asserted by TestUnconfiguredCallerMakesNoContentsCall rather than argued. A reviewer should check that claim first, because it is what bounds everything else. Enumerate with a NESTED walk of default_config, not a top-level jsonb_each: loop sub_workflows hide steps from the shallow query. PLACEMENT OBJECTION, pre-empted: LANDMINES says the owned-page guard does NOT belong on git_commit. That entry concerns a guard refusing a CLASS OF CALLER, which broke legitimate deploy paths and looked like 'tools mysteriously stopped updating'; this refuses a SHAPE OF PAYLOAD, only for a step that asked, and names both sizes in the refusal. If the council disagrees, the contained alternative is to enforce only when the caller ALSO passes an explicit allow-list of paths — more config for the same outcome. OPTIONAL-KEY SURFACE, disclosed rather than hidden: git_commit carries 10 ad-hoc config keys today and has NO RegisterActionInputSpec, so cmd/config-key-audit lists it under censusUncountedActions ('optional surface is UNKNOWABLE, not zero') and the RFC_022 budget of N=10 cannot see it. file_shrink_floor is the 11th. Registering a spec would turn unrecognised keys into warnings across 19 live steps and is a separate change; a review doc enumerating all 11 keys ships with the Go commit, and per RFC_022 (owner 2026-08-11) an opt-in field whose unsafe default is OFF with zero live consumers naming it is not architecture-scope. STATUS SEMANTICS CHANGE: css-patch-agent items that previously read 'complete' will now read needs_human_review (refusals) or failed (errors). This is the point — the old rows were false — but anything counting completions for this handler will see the number drop, and 296's parked-findings census should be re-taken after this lands rather than compared across it. A parked row HOLDS its dedup key, so the same finding cannot re-file while parked; the unpark sweep keys on result->>'parked_by' and is in the workstream RUNBOOK. The 'failed' arm goes through applyWorkItemFailureLadder, so a transient error retries with backoff rather than dying on first failure. PERSIST STEP FAILS OPEN by design (error_step: deploy_css): the realistic step error is an unresolvable site_context.site_id on a non-site run, and failing an entire design run over a bookkeeping write would trade a live capability for a hygiene property. The backstop is 542 — an unpersisted row causes a REFUSAL later, never a clobber. A 0-row match is a NORMAL outcome (shared row, seed row, unchanged content) and is recorded in css_persisted.count, not treated as an error. WHAT IS NOT COVERED: webdesign-agent's own deploy_css stays unguarded, because a genuine redesign may honestly shrink the file; the row now tracks it, and the consumer is guarded. Sites on a shared seed theme (finetuning.uk, gaswholesalers.com) are refused rather than fixed — they need a per-site theme split, which is a human decision flagged for the owner. Candidate 6 (refuse when the offending declaration is not in the theme the agent can edit — three sites' evidence: H3.H3 on dartsonline, p.P twice on remortgagecalculator) is deliberately a separate task. ORDERING: config is live on apply; the Go half is inert until BOTH the chassis and git-adapter images roll, and each half alone is a no-op, so no ordering constraint is claimed.
